source.title: Towards Federated Learning against Noisy Labels via Local Self-Regularization
source.authors: Xue Jiang; Sheng Sun; Yuwei Wang; Min Liu

page_placements.theme: Federated training changes memorization and generalization trajectories

record.tranche_reason: Tests performance under varying noisy-label rates in federated learning, but does not measure training error on random labels.
record.gate_note: The paper reports cited memorization findings from prior work, which are not rows. Its own results report test accuracy under synthetic symmetric and pairwise label noise; training error is not reported.
record.test_reason: The federated-learning noise sweep tests V4's test-error degradation component: FedAvg test accuracy decreases monotonically as symmetric label noise increases. It does not establish perfect training fit or directly measure the clean-before-noisy learning order in V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately describes the authors' interpretation: they infer memorization in federated learning from an initial rise and later decline in test accuracy. Their main conclusion is that Local Self-Regularization improves robustness to noisy labels. The reported trajectories do not directly verify clean-before-noisy training fit.
record.recipe_differences: Federated learning experiments with synthetic symmetric and pairwise label noise; the study does not reproduce the original random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, noise type and ratio, augmentation, and IID versus non-IID data partitioning affect reported test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.2 reports that noisy-label FedAvg test accuracy initially rises and subsequently declines; Fashion-MNIST has an approximately 20-round warm-up period.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Federated learning on noisy labels can exhibit early improvement followed by deterioration in held-out accuracy. This trajectory alone does not establish that clean training labels are fitted before noisy ones.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM ’22)
record.problems: The study reports test accuracy, not training error, so it cannot establish whether these models fit the noisy training labels. Some comparator results in Table 8 are quoted from prior work.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: the reported outcomes are test accuracy under label noise, without a reported training-fit measure, so they do not establish the central behavior in V4 or the fitting behavior in V1.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error on completely random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged training hyperparameters.
Time required to fit random versus true labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit throughout the corruption sweep and behavior through complete randomization. Symmetric corruption reaches only 70%; training error is not reported.
Whether conventional regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing it preserves true-label generalization.
Separate learning trajectories for correctly and incorrectly labeled training examples. Rising then falling test accuracy does not directly establish their learning order.

missing.what: Add FedAvg symmetric-noise test-accuracy rows for V4's degradation component. The blanket exclusion in rows_left_out incorrectly treats missing training error as making test-error results irrelevant. At noise fractions 0.3/0.4/0.5/0.6/0.7, accuracies are MNIST: 91.34/83.53/73.60/57.86/42.12%; Fashion-MNIST: 80.02/72.75/62.29/49.22/35.87%; CIFAR-10: 53.78/46.06/36.93/28.45/19.80%.

record.verdict_notes: Support for V4 is restricted to its measured test-error component. Neither absent training-error measurements nor mitigation improvements warrant a challenge or scope-limit verdict about random-label fitting.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, training error, chance test error, and comparison with the same network on true labels.
Training time, convergence speed, and how convergence changes with corrupted-label fraction.
Shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
The paper varies label-noise ratios and reports test accuracy, but does not report training error or show that training fit stays perfect while test error rises.
Whether regularization or augmentation prevents fitting random labels, and whether removing them harms generalization on true labels.
Whether true patterns are learned before noisy labels, or how real and random labels differ over training.

relationships.condition: FedAvg with IID partitions, 9-layer CNN, symmetric label noise from 30% to 70%, on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10; test-error component only.
relationships.reason: Table 3 in the supplied text shows monotonically falling test accuracy: 91.34% to 42.12%, 80.02% to 35.87%, and 53.78% to 19.80%, respectively. This supports increasing test error over the tested interval; no extracted row ids exist.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy fell monotonically from 91.34% to 42.12% on MNIST, 80.02% to 35.87% on Fashion-MNIST, and 53.78% to 19.80% on CIFAR-10.
